messages:
maria: Opening a small docs thread to tidy up Dedicated capacity docs: explicit autoscale examples, SLA language, and a short migration checklist.
ton: thanks  Can you paste the PR link?
maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/449
sean: skimmed. Autoscale section needs a concrete example that contrasts pre-alloc vs burst. Customers get confused about billing during bursts.
anya: also call out that "isolation" covers compute tenancy and network/VPC separation separately. People often assume GPU tenancy implies VPC isolation.
maria: good point. I'll add a short callout and a one-liner about KMS/HSM for Private.
sean: suggested autoscale snippet: ```yaml
# example autoscale policy
policy:
  target_utilization: 0.6
  scale_up: 2
  scale_down: 1
  burst_capacity: true
```
ton: nit: use `capacityCommitment` in examples to match SDK naming. Also add a short JS SDK example for creating a pool.
maria: added JS example: ```js
await client.dedicated.createPool({
  name: 'prod-gpu',
  gpus: 4,
  capacityCommitment: 0.5
});
```
anya: SLA language: don't promise no evictions. Suggest: "We provide best-effort eviction protection for reserved pools; in overload scenarios, requests may fallback to compatible model variants or lower priority pools."
sean: fine. Also include suggested monitoring queries for latency and eviction rate. Small grafana snippet would help.
maria: added grafana query examples and a short migration checklist: rotate API keys, update endpoint from api.redwood to dedicated.redwood, pin model version, warm prefix cache.
infra-bot: preview build created: https://deploy-preview.redwood.dev/449 (visual diffs + link checker)
ton: link check failed on an old internal KB link. Please swap to the public billing page.
maria: swapped link, fixed wording on eviction mitigation steps, and pushed.
anya: LGTM from security side.
sean: +1 for docs. Approving.
maria: thanks y'all, merging after CI. I'll follow up if any support tickets come in.
